name: Olivia Rodrigo
label: Geffen
lede: Olivia Rodrigo wrote a Disney+ song in three days, signed a record deal off it, and has since opened every album cycle with a number one single.

eras.title: A kid from Temecula with a guitar
eras.text: Rodrigo grew up in a Riverside County suburb, took vocal lessons at five and piano at nine, and picked up guitar around twelve after falling for Taylor Swift. Disney Channel got to her before radio did.

years.h: An only child in Temecula, with lessons from age five
years.p: Olivia Rodrigo was born in Murrieta. Her mother, Jennifer, teaches school; her father, Chris, is a family therapist of Filipino descent.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists vocal lessons at age five, piano at nine and guitar around twelve. Songwriting started in earnest after she got into Taylor Swift, whom she has called her biggest fan.

She is partially deaf in her left ear, a detail she has mentioned herself in interviews and that Wikipedia records.

years.h: Disney Channel hires her as a guitarist
years.p: Rodrigo played Paige Olvera on Bizaardvark from 2016 to 2019, moved to Los Angeles for the part and finished school through homeschooling.

eras.title: Nini writes a song in three days
eras.text: A Disney+ musical series turned a working actress into a songwriter with a label problem: everybody wanted her. She picked the one that would let her own her masters.

years.h: Cast as Nini, the girl with the songbook
years.p: Rodrigo played Nini Salazar-Roberts in the Disney+ mockumentary High School Musical: The Musical: The Series, which premiered in November 2019.

years.src: Wikipedia: All I Want (Olivia Rodrigo song)
years.h: Three days to write "All I Want", then a record deal
years.p: The song about Nini's boy troubles took off on TikTok and downloads. Wikipedia says that pulled in a recording contract with Interscope.
years.xp: Rodrigo says she wrote it while shooting season one, and Matthew Tishler produced. It plays in the fourth episode, "Blocking".

years.src: Wikipedia: Sour (Olivia Rodrigo album) · Wikipedia: Dan Nigro · Wikipedia: As Tall as Lions
years.h: A DM from Dan Nigro starts the partnership behind three albums
years.p: A mutual friend played Nigro her songs from the High School Musical: The Musical: The Series soundtrack. He messaged her on Instagram and they started writing.
years.xp:
Nigro was not a pop producer by origin. He fronted [[As Tall as Lions|71f17703-cd11-4579-b08a-1b1c8e6f5ac2]], formed in December 2001 in Massapequa, New York, signed to Island and Triple Crown, made three albums from Lafcadio (2004) to You Can't Take It with You (2009), and split on September 29, 2010.

He went on to work with Sky Ferreira, [[Chappell Roan|56a55378-f155-48de-80a5-d80104221267]] (whom he signed to his Amusement Records), Conan Gray and Caroline Polachek. Wikipedia counts two Grammy wins, one of them Producer of the Year in 2025.

years.cap: Rodrigo with President Biden recording a vaccine PSA at the White House
years.h: Geffen signs her, and she keeps her masters
years.p: Rodrigo signed with Interscope's Geffen Records and, per Wikipedia, negotiated ownership of her master recordings. She has said Interscope's John Janick praised her songwriting over her star quality.

eras.title: One January, one song, no going back
eras.text: "Drivers License" reset her life in a week, and by summer the debut album had rewritten the credits on three of its songs. The Grammys, the White House and Glastonbury followed in a year.

years.cap: Rodrigo with Vice President Kamala Harris at the White House, July 14, 2021
years.src: Wikipedia: Drivers License (song) · Wikipedia: Olivia Rodrigo
years.h: "Drivers License" goes straight to number one and Spotify's record falls
years.p: Written with Dan Nigro at Amusement Studios in Los Angeles. It debuted at #1 on the Hot 100, making Rodrigo the youngest artist to debut atop it, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
She announced it on January 4 and released it January 8. It broke Spotify's record for single-day streams of a non-holiday song by day four and stayed at #1 for eight weeks.

Media speculation about the ex and the co-stars it might refer to poured fuel on it. The video was directed by Matthew Dillon Cohen and shot in Provo, Utah.

years.h: The "Good 4 U" video raids Audition and Jennifer's Body
years.p: Petra Collins directed it at Palisades Charter High School. The song debuted at #1 on the Hot 100 and topped charts in 23 countries.
years.xp: Rodrigo and Nigro wrote it, and Nigro produced with Alexander 23 at Amusement Studios. The video pulls from horror films Audition (1999) and Jennifer's Body (2009), plus the comedy The Princess Diaries (2001).

years.src: Wikipedia: Sour (Olivia Rodrigo album) · Wikipedia: Olivia Rodrigo
years.h: Sour opens at number one and stays five weeks
years.p: Nigro produced the debut over 2020 and early 2021. Wikipedia calls it the longest-reigning #1 by a woman in 2021.
years.xp:
Announced April 1 under the working title OR, retitled April 13. Nigro and Rodrigo worked out how to make it safely in isolation during the pandemic.

Companions: Sour Prom, a concert film on YouTube in June 2021, and the Disney+ documentary Driving Home 2 U on March 25, 2022.

years.big: All music is inspired by each other.
years.src: Wikipedia: Sour (Olivia Rodrigo album) · Wikipedia: Deja Vu (Olivia Rodrigo song) · Wikipedia: Good 4 U
years.h: Swift and Paramore get songwriting credits on Sour
years.p: Olivia Rodrigo's answer to the argument over "Deja Vu", which added Taylor Swift, Jack Antonoff and St. Vincent in July, and "Good 4 U", which added Hayley Williams and Josh Farro of Paramore in August.
years.xp:
"Deja Vu" credits Swift, [[Jack Antonoff|1155a7a9-a7b4-46ba-ba27-6b6c98be487e]] and [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]] for its bridge nod to "Cruel Summer"; "Good 4 U" credits [[Hayley Williams|b4b5b5a7-feff-47d0-9458-83d0d135a692]] and [[Josh Farro|7365489a-815a-43f3-b361-26a091227f98]] of [[Paramore|44cf61b8-5197-448a-b82b-cef6ee89fac5]] for "Misery Business". "1 Step Forward, 3 Steps Back" also carries Swift and Antonoff credits, for its "New Year's Day" piano line.

Wikipedia reports Rodrigo's team had contacted Williams and Farro before "Good 4 U" came out, and that they took a combined 50% royalty share, reported at between $700,000 and $1.2 million. Fans argued it both ways.

years.h: The Grammys hand her three wins from seven nominations
years.p: At the 64th Grammys, Rodrigo took Best New Artist, Best Pop Vocal Album for Sour and Best Pop Solo Performance for "Drivers License".

years.cap: Rodrigo on the Sour Tour, Toronto, April 29, 2022
years.h: At Glastonbury, Rodrigo dedicates "Fuck You" to the Supreme Court
years.p: On the Sour Tour she brought out [[Lily Allen|6e0c7c0e-cba5-4c2c-a652-38f71ef5785d]] for the song of that name and aimed it at the justices who overturned Roe v. Wade.

years.h: "Lacy" starts as a poetry class assignment at USC
years.p: Rodrigo's homework became "Lacy", a track on Guts.

eras.title: Distortion, arenas and a visit from Robert Smith
eras.text: The second album traded ballads for distorted guitars and a stage show that filled arenas for sixteen months. Then Glastonbury put her onstage with the man whose band she would spend the next record circling.

years.h: Her third number one debut, "Vampire", starts as a piano ballad
years.p: Dan Nigro produced and played most of it. Rodrigo calls it their "version of a rock opera", with big drums and tempo changes added along the way.
years.xp: Nigro played guitar, percussion, piano, bass and synth. It logged 35.5 million streams in its first week. Petra Collins's video won the MTV VMA for Best Editing.

years.src: Wikipedia: Guts (album) · Wikipedia: Get Him Back!
years.h: Guts opens at 302,000 units with all 12 tracks in the top 40
years.p: Nigro produced again, largely at Amusement Studios in Los Angeles. Rock songs were picked by how the crowd reacted live.
years.xp: Metacritic scored it 91. The "Get Him Back!" video came out September 12: eight Rodrigo clones wrecking an ex's house, shot on an iPhone 15 Pro Max by director Jack Begert.

years.cap: Rodrigo at The O2, London, May 15, 2024
years.h: The Guts World Tour starts in Thousand Palms, California
years.p: Openers rotated through [[Chappell Roan|56a55378-f155-48de-80a5-d80104221267]], [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]], [[PinkPantheress|7441014f-f8f5-494f-81db-ff166fbc078d]], [[Beabadoobee|88d17133-abbc-42db-9526-4e2c1db60336]] and [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]] before the run ended July 1, 2025 in Manchester.
years.xp: Wikipedia counts 102 shows, four of them at London's O2 Arena, and puts the gross at $208.6 million across 101 reported shows, the highest for an artist born in the 21st century. Mexico City's Estadio GNP Seguros drew 114,168.

years.h: At Coachella she sings "Bathwater" with No Doubt
years.p: Rodrigo grew up on [[No Doubt|fbd2a255-1d57-4d31-ac11-65b671c19958]], and joined them onstage for the song during their Coachella set.

years.cap: Rodrigo on stage at Glastonbury, June 29, 2025
years.src: Ultimate Classic Rock: Robert Smith · Wikipedia: Live from Glastonbury (A BBC Recording)
yt: Just Like Heaven with Robert Smith, Glastonbury 2025
years.h: Rodrigo headlines Glastonbury and brings out Robert Smith
years.p: [[Robert Smith|7d1a1624-784b-4f89-8ff9-b9b493cd059d]] of [[The Cure|69ee3720-a7cb-4402-b48d-a02c366f2bcf]] joined her on the Pyramid Stage for "Just Like Heaven" and "Friday I'm in Love".
years.xp:
She introduced him as perhaps the best songwriter to come out of England and "a personal hero of mine," per Ultimate Classic Rock.

The Guardian gave the show five stars.

years.src: Wikipedia: Live from Glastonbury (A BBC Recording)
years.h: The Glastonbury set becomes her first live album
years.p: Recorded June 29, it followed a double single of the Smith duets, announced September 8, with proceeds going to Doctors Without Borders.

eras.title: Synths, Versailles and a record that splits in two
eras.text: Written after time in London, her third album swapped guitars for synths and post-punk references. It is her most argued-over record and, per Pitchfork, her most adventurous.

years.h: "Drop Dead" debuts at number one, with a video shot at Versailles
years.p: [[Amy Allen|4d41868f-8901-4e77-bbd9-ead5bb7831ee]] and Nigro co-wrote the synth-pop lead single. Rodrigo debuted it at Coachella on April 18 as a guest of [[Addison Rae|610b71d9-fa78-47d6-9073-083922e73840]]; Petra Collins directed the video.
years.xp: Arranged with strings by Paul Cartwright. It made Rodrigo the first artist whose lead singles from three studio albums all reached #1.

years.cap: Rodrigo on the SNL swing with Weyes Blood, May 2, 2026
years.h: Rodrigo hosts SNL and debuts "Begged" from a swing
years.p: [[Weyes Blood|469d6414-1f06-43de-80d5-17762d4a356a]] sang backup on the ballad, which followed her performance of "Drop Dead".

years.h: "The Cure" is not about the Cure
years.p: Rodrigo says the second single has nothing to do with the band. Pitchfork named it Best New Track.

years.src: Wikipedia: You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love · Olivia Rodrigo Charts on X
years.h: Pitchfork gives her third album an 8.3 and Best New Music
years.p: The first seven tracks are about being in love; the last six are about it going wrong. Robert Smith sings on "What's Wrong with Me".
years.xp:
Released June 12 on Geffen, it debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200 with 485,000 units and topped the UK chart. Pitchfork's Molly Mary O'Brien called it Rodrigo's most sophisticated work, and it earned Best New Music.

Third single "Stupid Song" followed July 13. Rodrigo cited The Cure, New Order, Depeche Mode and Siouxsie and the Banshees, and called [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] and [[Courtney Love|31d2041c-985d-48f7-b6e2-2a70cdf14853]] her heroes.
play: you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love

years.src: Wikipedia: You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love
years.h: Hartford opens the 86-date Unraveled Tour
years.p: It runs through May 10, 2027 in London, with [[Wolf Alice|3547f34a-db02-4ab7-b4a0-380e1ef951a9]] and [[The Last Dinner Party|2f0c90b1-84d5-47f1-ad75-ad8d30f53f70]] among the supports.
